trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out down-right, left or right yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-right.
I can't rule out up-right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up-right.
The line must go right: down-right is number 7, which comes later.
I can't rule out left or down-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
I can't rule out down-right or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: down-right.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-left.
Going down-left would leave number 6 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-left.
Going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up-left.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down-left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1); going down-right, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes left.

Going up-left would force the line onto number 14 before its turn; going left, the next 9 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-3,3) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-right.
Going left would leave number 10 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes right.
Number 10 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Cell (0,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going up-right would wall in number 15, the last number. So the line goes up-left.
Going up-right would leave both cell (-3,0) and cell (-2,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would wall in number 15, the last number. So the line goes up-left.
Going right would cut off the bottom-left corner (2 cells). So the line goes up-right.
Going right would leave both number 14 and cell (-2,0) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going down-right would cut off the bottom-left corner (2 cells). So the line goes up-right.
Cell (0,-3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going down-left would turn number 14 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
